description: Beyond Pulse is building thoughtful health technology for crews working far from Earth, connecting personal health signals with clear guidance and a trusted medical support network.
summary: Beyond Pulse is a crew-centered health-monitoring prototype built around Maya, a fictional astronaut on a long-duration mission. It brings her simulated health trends, wellbeing, activity, body-health observations, daily routine, and mission context into one interface. Historical NASA OSDR RadLab radiation data and NASA EDA environmental archive data appear separately from Maya’s simulated readings, with source labels throughout. The quantitative-ultrasound (QUS) view records speed-of-sound (SOS) observations only; it does not estimate bone mineral density. An optional, consent-gated AI brief summarizes selected synthetic values, while the medical-support workflow lets the user review and export a handoff. Beyond Pulse explores how source-aware software can help crew understand changes and communicate clearly. This prototype does not connect to NASA flight sensors, diagnose, or send medical data automatically.
details:
Beyond Pulse is a browser-based health workspace for Maya, a fictional astronaut. Its home and trends views organize a seven-day simulated mission scenario; wellness, activity, and daily-plan views bring related crew tasks together. The body-health view records quantitative-ultrasound speed-of-sound observations without converting them into a bone-density result. The environment view keeps historical NASA OSDR RadLab and EDA archive records separate from Maya’s fictional health values. An optional AI brief can summarize selected scenario values after the user consents, and Medical Support lets the user review and export a handoff.

The prototype uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interface and a Python standard-library server for local hosting and NASA archive requests. Its design emphasizes clear source labels, simple trends, and a user-reviewed care handoff. The app uses no NASA flight hardware or live crew sensor feed, has no clinical validation, and is not a diagnostic tool.
